identity.name: ICICI BANK LTD.
identity.industry: Private-Sector Bank (universal — retail + corporate + rural + international; + insurance / AMC / securities subs)

summary.oneLiner: ICICI Bank is a leading Indian private-sector bank delivering a full suite of financial products and services, anchored by a strong deposit franchise and a granular, risk-calibrated loan portfolio.
summary.business: ICICI Bank offers a comprehensive range of banking and financial services to retail, corporate, and institutional clients, including lending, deposit-taking, wealth management, insurance, and asset management. It operates through an extensive branch and digital network, serving customers across India and select international markets. The Bank's subsidiaries and associates span life and general insurance, asset management, and venture funds, enabling a unified 'One Bank, One Team' approach.

currentContext.strengths: Strong liability franchise with stable CASA deposit base (average CASA ratio ~38.9% in FY2026) providing a competitive cost-of-funds advantage|Granular, diversified loan portfolio with no specific segment-wise targets, emphasizing risk-calibrated growth and 'Return of Capital'|Robust capital adequacy (CET-1 ratio of 16.35% and total CAR of 17.18% as of March 2026, well above regulatory requirements)|Extensive distribution network with 7,511 branches and 12,087 ATMs/CRMs, complemented by significant technology and cybersecurity investments|Integrated financial services ecosystem through subsidiaries and associates (ICICI Prudential Life, ICICI Lombard, ICICI Prudential AMC, ICICI Venture) enabling cross-sell and customer 360-degree coverage
currentContext.strategies: Focus on risk-calibrated profitable growth by optimising all levers of profitability while capitalising on market opportunities.|Prioritise 'Return of Capital' through selection of right counterparties and conservation of capital.|Strengthen delivery systems through simplified processes, enhanced data analytics, and leveraging digital public infrastructure.|Adopt 'Agile Risk Management' to proactively identify, assess, and mitigate risks.|Deepen presence across large ecosystems and customer segments (multinational corporations, global capability centres, new-age companies, NRIs, senior citizens) in a unified 'One Bank, One Team' manner.|Enhance retail deposit franchise and garner low-cost deposits to maintain competitive advantage in cost of funds.|Maximise profit before tax excluding treasury within guardrails of compliance and risk management.|Grow loan portfolio in a granular manner with focus on risk and reward, without specific targets for loan mix or segment-wise loan growth.|Invest in technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, and thoughtful adoption of AI/Gen AI while ensuring data privacy and cybersecurity guardrails.|Maintain a strong balance sheet with prudent provisioning, healthy capital adequacy, and adequate liquidity.|The Bank has a Dividend Distribution Policy hosted on its website in accordance with SEBI Listing Regulations. The policy governs the philosophy for dividend payouts. The Bank raised funds through issue of unsecured, subordinated, listed, non-convertible, Tier 2, Basel III compliant bonds during fiscal 2026, with no deviation in utilisation of funds.|CSR commitment of ₹9.94 billion in FY2026, with nearly half allocated to healthcare (non-communicable diseases, cancer and cardiac care) and ~17% each to environment/ecology and rural entrepreneurship.|Flagship greenfield cancer-care and research facilities being set up in collaboration with Tata Memorial Hospitals; foundation stones laid in Visakhapatnam and Navi Mumbai in FY2026.|Water security initiatives have enabled creation of 34 billion litres of water storage/recharge capacity cumulatively; watershed development undertaken over 4,200 hectares in FY2026.|GhanVan biodiversity restoration programme in collaboration with Tata Power, providing insights on climate-resilient plantation; initiatives undertaken in about 83 forests and national parks.|Self-Help Group programme has supported over 12.3 million women since inception with cumulative funding exceeding ₹35,500 crore; ~81,000 SHGs financed in FY2026, 79% repeat borrowers.|Financed 53,073 farmers for farm equipment in FY2026, of which 65% were small and marginal farmers, contributing to mechanisation of small holdings.
currentContext.expansion: The Bank does not describe specific plant, smelter, or mine capex projects. Its expansion narrative is focused on strategic investments in technology and cybersecurity to strengthen operational infrastructure, ensuring scalability and robustness, and on deepening presence across ecosystems and micro markets in a unified manner. The Bank continues to make investments in technology and cybersecurity as part of its ongoing operational resilience and delivery system enhancements.
currentContext.mdna: India GDP growth at 7.7% in fiscal 2026, driven by domestic demand, private consumption, and steady investment activity.|RBI policy rate cuts of 100 bps during fiscal 2026 lowered cost of borrowing, supporting consumption revival.|Banking system non-food credit grew 16.1% YoY, driven by services (19% YoY), personal credit (6.2% YoY), and industry credit (15% YoY).|Deposit growth for SCBs picked up to 13.5% YoY, improving funding environment.|Medium-term growth prospects remain positive, supported by structural reforms and policy measures, though global tariff uncertainty and geopolitical developments could weigh on outlook.|RBI projects GDP growth for fiscal 2027 at approximately 6.9%, supported by strong domestic demand, services sector, higher manufacturing capacity utilisation, and government measures to boost domestic manufacturing.|RBI projects CPI inflation for fiscal 2027 at 4.6%, with upside pressure from higher global energy prices and concerns of below-normal monsoon; core inflation remains benign.|Ongoing West Asia conflict poses heightened uncertainty, potential supply-chain disruptions, and upward pressure on energy and commodity prices.|Rupee depreciation of ~10.9% during fiscal 2026 and decline in equity markets (Sensex -7.06%) reflect external headwinds.|Bank expects to continue participating in opportunities by leveraging market standing and prioritising long-term sustainable value creation.

risks.risk: Global tariff uncertainty and geopolitical developments
risks.note: Could weigh on India's medium-term growth prospects, impacting credit demand and asset quality across the Bank's portfolio.

risks.risk: Volatility in global financial markets and weather-related events
risks.note: Poses downside risk to domestic growth outlook; weather events like El NiÃ±o can disrupt food prices and rural incomes, affecting agricultural and MSME loan books.
Heightened uncertainty for the global economy, potential supply-chain disruptions, and upward pressure on energy and commodity prices, which could fuel inflation and force tighter monetary policy.

risks.risk: Inflation resurgence and higher global energy prices
risks.note: RBI projects CPI at 4.6% for FY2027; upside pressure from energy and below-normal monsoon could erode household savings and loan repayment capacity.

risks.risk: Rupee depreciation and rising bond yields
risks.note: Rupee depreciated ~10.9% in FY2026; 10-year G-sec yield rose to 7.04%. Sustained depreciation and higher yields can increase the cost of foreign-currency borrowings and mark-to-market hits on the investment portfolio.
As a systemically important bank, failure in technology, cybersecurity, or delivery systems could disrupt operations, erode customer trust, and attract regulatory sanction.

risks.risk: Concentration in unsecured retail or granular credit segments
risks.note: While the Bank focuses on granular loan growth, rapid expansion in personal credit (system grew 6.2% YoY) without adequate risk-pricing could lead to higher slippages in a downturn.

one-line thesis: A clean, high-quality beat: PBT-excluding-treasury (management's headline KPI) grew +20.9% YoY, PAT +15.9%, standalone RoE 17.1%, and NIM *expanded* to 4.36% (industry-leading; ~4.28% ex a one-off tax-refund benefit) even as most peers compressed. The stand-out is a broad, accelerating loan book (+19.6% YoY / +5.0% QoQ — fastest in several quarters) led by a corporate rebound (+18.5%, partly bond-market substitution + working-capital) plus rural +35.4% and business banking +28.2%, on benign asset quality (net NPA 0.35%, normalised credit cost ~50 bps). Management stays deliberately guidance-shy — no loan-growth, NIM or FCNR-B targets — and frames everything as maximising risk-calibrated PBT-ex-treasury through multiple levers. FCNR(B) mobilisation has just begun (marginally NIM-dilutive, earnings-accretive).

| NIM | 4.36% | vs 4.32% Q4FY26 / 4.34% Q1FY26 | ex tax-refund benefit (8 bps): **4.28%** (vs 4.27% / 4.27%) — genuinely stable-to-up |
| Fee income | Rs 7,286 cr | +23.5% | off a low Q1FY26 base; retail/rural/BB = ~72% of fees |

| Opex | Rs 12,574 cr | +10.4% | employee +5.5% (increments/promotions); non-employee +13.8%; tech = 11.4% of opex |
| Provisions | Rs 1,260 cr | vs Rs 1,815 cr Q1FY26 | 6.2% of core op profit; 0.32% of avg advances |
| PBT ex-treasury | Rs 18,975 cr | +20.9% | management's primary KPI |
| PAT (standalone) | Rs 14,805 cr | +15.9% | incl. Rs 446 cr tax write-back (favourable orders) |
| PAT (consolidated) | Rs 15,440 cr | +13.9% | |
| RoE (standalone) | 17.1% | — | |
| Net NPA | 0.35% | vs 0.33% Mar / 0.41% Jun-25 | GNPA additions Rs 5,552 cr; recoveries/upgrades Rs 2,845 cr; net add Rs 2,707 cr; PCR 74.7% |
| Deposits (period-end) | +14.0% YoY / +2.2% QoQ | — | avg deposits +14.0% YoY / +6.1% QoQ; avg CASA +12.1% YoY |
| Total advances | +19.6% YoY / +5.0% QoQ | — | domestic +18.8%; overseas 3.1% of book |
| Capital | CET-1 16.19% · CAR 16.84% | — | net worth ~Rs 3.5 lakh cr; contingency provisions Rs 13,100 cr |
> One-offs to normalise: **+8 bps** NIM from interest on income-tax refund (vs 5 bps Q4, 7 bps Q1FY26); **Rs 446 cr** tax write-back on favourable orders; treasury gain Rs 151 cr (vs Rs 1,241 cr gain Q1FY26). Credit cost flattered by a chunky NCLT recovery (asset previously sold to NARCL) — normalised ~50 bps vs reported 32 bps.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Loan growth:** explicitly NO target ("we do not give guidance on any segment"); momentum "pretty strong"; average (vs period-end) YoY growth will be somewhat lower — some base effect + lumpiness in the 19.6%.
- **NIM:** expected **range-bound in FY27 assuming no policy-rate movements**; FCNR(B) programme + loans-against-FCNR "slightly NIM-dilutive" but earnings-accretive (offshore B/S expansion).
- **FCNR(B) / overseas funding:** NO quantum target; a **~USD 2.5 bn overseas bond borrowing programme** has enabling approval (not yet tapped — "each bank has its own timing"); FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging ~**6.30–6.40%** (< wholesale). Will "leverage" via partner banks + own bond raises; committed to making the RBI/government scheme a success; a "full picture" at Q2 results.
- **Credit cost:** reported ~30–32 bps this quarter; **normalised level ~50 bps**, "where it stays."
- **ECL transition (effective 1-Apr-2027):** **no material net-worth impact** expected at transition (absorbed by existing buffers); ongoing higher Stage-2 provisions partly offset by lower Stage-3; uniform across sector adjusted for portfolio mix. Won't quantify.
- **Agri/KCC provision:** remediation of the portfolio in progress; write-back of the Rs 1,283 cr RBI-directed agri provision "over the next few months" — no timeline committed.
order book & pipeline (loan pipeline / g:
- Corporate the swing factor: sequential pickup (+18.5% YoY, +6.9% QoQ) from working-capital demand + substitution out of a soft bond/equity market; "healthy pipeline at reasonable rates"; no meaningful *fresh-capex* step-up called out (management reluctant to extrapolate to system level).
- Rural +35.4% YoY (gold loan a substantial part; sits inside rural, not PL); business banking +28.2% (granular, secured; ECLGS applications being assessed); mortgage +14.6%; personal loans +12.9% (after a long time back to 4% QoQ); auto +3.6%; CV/equipment +12.8%; cards **-1.9%** (lower revolver rates).
- NBFC/HFC exposure Rs 92,052 cr (4.5% of advances); builder book Rs 74,721 cr (4.3%, largely well-established; only 0.7% BB-and-below/NPA).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Deposits/funding:** cost of deposits 4.41% (vs 4.43% Q4, 4.85% Q1FY26); LCR 124% (vs 128% a year ago); ~57% of domestic loans repo/external-benchmark linked, 13% MCLR, 30% fixed.
- **Subsidiaries (Q1FY27 PAT):** ICICI Life APE Rs 2,136 cr, VNB Rs 571 cr (margin 26.7% vs 24.7%), PAT Rs 386 cr; ICICI General GDPI Rs 8,318 cr, PAT Rs 403 cr (down on reserve increase from a judicial pronouncement; combined ratio 107.2%); ICICI AMC PAT Rs 965 cr (+23%); ICICI Securities PAT Rs 419 cr; ICICI Home Finance PAT Rs 200 cr; ICICI Bank Canada CAD 5.3 mn; ICICI Bank UK USD 7.2 mn.
- **Asset quality detail:** KCC GNPA additions Rs 706 cr (seasonal Q1/Q3); retail+rural gross additions Rs 4,331 cr (down YoY); corporate+BB net additions Rs 586 cr; BB-and-below performing corporate Rs 3,485 cr (0.2% of advances); resolution book down to Rs 1,363 cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **FCNR(B) window:** leverages ICICI's large international presence (West Asia branches) + diaspora; earnings-accretive via offshore balance-sheet expansion; product/rates to evolve over the next 8–10 weeks.
- **AI / GenAI:** enterprise AI platform live; use-cases in portfolio monitoring, onboarding, fraud detection, document extraction/summarisation, servicing; deliberately calibrated ("no hurry to be a pioneer"), governance-first, human-in-the-loop; no material headcount impact expected — benefits must show up in PBT.
- Cross-sell / 360-degree ecosystem framing across corporate + business-banking + retail micromarkets remains the operating model.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM 4.36% (4.28% clean) held up on funding-franchise strength + disciplined deposit/loan pricing + G-sec book management, despite KCC interest reversals and corporate-mix growth (yields sustained). Cost of deposits still repricing down (4.85%→4.41% YoY).
- Forward NIM gated by systemic liquidity/rates (May wholesale-rate hardening has since reversed) and the FCNR(B) dilution — net "range-bound." Opex growth (10.4%) below FY26's 11.5%; positive jaws.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Distribution: 97 branches added in Q1 → 7,608 branches, 12,190 ATMs/CRMs. No large physical-expansion guidance; investment weighted to technology/AI (11.4% of opex).
capital allocation: - Strong organic capital (CET-1 16.19%); "Return of Capital" a stated guiding principle. Contingency provisions held at Rs 13,100 cr (~0.8% of advances) — conservative buffer maintained. No buyback/dividend specifics on the call. Growth funded within risk-calibrated-profit framework.
risks & watch-items:
- **Geopolitics / West Asia** energy-shock + El Niño flagged by analysts as macro risks to business-banking/retail asset quality; management "comfortable" but monitoring customer selection.
- **FCNR(B) execution & NIM drag** — quantum unknown, dilution "to be seen"; competitive leverage (peers offering 9–12%) — ICICI deliberately "calibrated," won't over-lever.
- **Seasonal NPA** from KCC/agri in Q1/Q3; agri provision write-back timing uncertain.
- **Cards** book shrinking (revolver rates low); PL sustainability of 4% QoQ not guided.
- **ECL adoption 1-Apr-2027** — ongoing credit-cost uplift (immaterial per mgmt; verify).
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, repetitive-on-purpose. Consistent refusal to give segment targets ("we look at good-quality customers wherever risk/reward/pricing thresholds are met") and steered every FCNR question to "early days, full picture at Q2." Emphasised PBT-ex-treasury as the north star and "risk-calibrated profitable growth" over headline loan-growth optics. Candid that the strong quarter had identifiable tailwinds (tax-refund NIM benefit, chunky NCLT recovery, low fee base) and normalised them proactively — a credibility positive.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The 4.36% NIM is flattered by 8 bps of tax-refund interest; the clean 4.28% is what's genuinely stable — still sector-best, but don't extrapolate 4.36%.
- Corporate-loan revival is **funding-mix substitution** (weak bond/equity markets pushing borrowers to banks) + working-capital + liquidity buffers — *not* primarily a fresh-capex cycle; management was explicit it won't extrapolate to a system capex call.
- ICICI is the *laggard* in tapping the overseas bond / FCNR-B window (peers already in) — a deliberate wait-for-spreads stance, not weakness; Q2 will reveal the mobilised quantum.
- Credit-card book is *shrinking* (-1.9% YoY) yet card PBT is up on lower credit costs — a quality-over-growth read.
- Contingency provisions untouched at Rs 13,100 cr — dry powder that makes reported credit costs (32 bps) understate the through-cycle picture (~50 bps).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ICICI Bank offers a comprehensive range of banking and financial services to retail, corporate, and institutional clients, including lending, deposit-taking, wealth management, insurance, and asset management. It operates through an extensive branch and digital network, serving customers across India and select international markets. The Bank's subsidiaries and associates span life and general insurance, asset management, and venture funds, enabling a unified 'One Bank, One Team' approach.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited — subsidiary: Material listed subsidiary of the Bank. Incorporated July 20, 2000 in Mumbai.
- India Infradebt Limited — associate: Associate company. ICICI Group holds 42.33% equity stake. Significant influence due to holding >20% voting power.
- Arteria Technologies Private Limited — associate: Associate company. ICICI Group holds 19.02% equity stake. Significant influence through voting power and board representation.
- Falcon Tyres Limited — associate: Associate company. ICICI Group holds 26.39% equity stake. Investment is temporary in nature; not consolidated.
- FISERV Merchant Solutions Private Limited — associate: Ceased to be an associate of the Bank on April 17, 2025.
- NIIT Institute of Finance Banking and Insurance Training Limited — associate: Ceased to be an associate of the Bank on June 11, 2025.
- ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited — related party: Executive Director Sandeep Batra serves as Non-executive Director. Executive Director Rakesh Jha serves as Non-executive Director.
- ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited — related party: Executive Director Sandeep Batra serves as Non-executive Director.
- ICICI Home Finance Company Limited — related party: Executive Director Rakesh Jha and Executive Director Ajay Kumar Gupta serve as Non-executive Directors.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Deposits/funding:** cost of deposits 4.41% (vs 4.43% Q4, 4.85% Q1FY26); LCR 124% (vs 128% a year ago); ~57% of domestic loans repo/external-benchmark linked, 13% MCLR, 30% fixed.
- **Subsidiaries (Q1FY27 PAT):** ICICI Life APE Rs 2,136 cr, VNB Rs 571 cr (margin 26.7% vs 24.7%), PAT Rs 386 cr; ICICI General GDPI Rs 8,318 cr, PAT Rs 403 cr (down on reserve increase from a judicial pronouncement; combined ratio 107.2%); ICICI AMC PAT Rs 965 cr (+23%); ICICI Securities PAT Rs 419 cr; ICICI Home Finance PAT Rs 200 cr; ICICI Bank Canada CAD 5.3 mn; ICICI Bank UK USD 7.2 mn.
- **Asset quality detail:** KCC GNPA additions Rs 706 cr (seasonal Q1/Q3); retail+rural gross additions Rs 4,331 cr (down YoY); corporate+BB net additions Rs 586 cr; BB-and-below performing corporate Rs 3,485 cr (0.2% of advances); resolution book down to Rs 1,363 cr.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Retail Banking:** Savings accounts, Current accounts, Term deposits, Home loans, Personal loans, Auto loans, Credit cards
- **Corporate & Institutional Banking:** Working capital finance, Term loans, Trade finance, Cash management, Treasury services

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline (loan pipeline / growth drivers)
order_book.body:
- Corporate the swing factor: sequential pickup (+18.5% YoY, +6.9% QoQ) from working-capital demand + substitution out of a soft bond/equity market; "healthy pipeline at reasonable rates"; no meaningful *fresh-capex* step-up called out (management reluctant to extrapolate to system level).
- Rural +35.4% YoY (gold loan a substantial part; sits inside rural, not PL); business banking +28.2% (granular, secured; ECLGS applications being assessed); mortgage +14.6%; personal loans +12.9% (after a long time back to 4% QoQ); auto +3.6%; CV/equipment +12.8%; cards **-1.9%** (lower revolver rates).
- NBFC/HFC exposure Rs 92,052 cr (4.5% of advances); builder book Rs 74,721 cr (4.3%, largely well-established; only 0.7% BB-and-below/NPA).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Loan growth:** explicitly NO target ("we do not give guidance on any segment"); momentum "pretty strong"; average (vs period-end) YoY growth will be somewhat lower — some base effect + lumpiness in the 19.6%.
- **NIM:** expected **range-bound in FY27 assuming no policy-rate movements**; FCNR(B) programme + loans-against-FCNR "slightly NIM-dilutive" but earnings-accretive (offshore B/S expansion).
- **FCNR(B) / overseas funding:** NO quantum target; a **~USD 2.5 bn overseas bond borrowing programme** has enabling approval (not yet tapped — "each bank has its own timing"); FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging ~**6.30–6.40%** (< wholesale). Will "leverage" via partner banks + own bond raises; committed to making the RBI/government scheme a success; a "full picture" at Q2 results.
- **Credit cost:** reported ~30–32 bps this quarter; **normalised level ~50 bps**, "where it stays."
- **ECL transition (effective 1-Apr-2027):** **no material net-worth impact** expected at transition (absorbed by existing buffers); ongoing higher Stage-2 provisions partly offset by lower Stage-3; uniform across sector adjusted for portfolio mix. Won't quantify.
- **Agri/KCC provision:** remediation of the portfolio in progress; write-back of the Rs 1,283 cr RBI-directed agri provision "over the next few months" — no timeline committed.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **FCNR(B) window:** leverages ICICI's large international presence (West Asia branches) + diaspora; earnings-accretive via offshore balance-sheet expansion; product/rates to evolve over the next 8–10 weeks.
- **AI / GenAI:** enterprise AI platform live; use-cases in portfolio monitoring, onboarding, fraud detection, document extraction/summarisation, servicing; deliberately calibrated ("no hurry to be a pioneer"), governance-first, human-in-the-loop; no material headcount impact expected — benefits must show up in PBT.
- Cross-sell / 360-degree ecosystem framing across corporate + business-banking + retail micromarkets remains the operating model.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India GDP growth at 7.7% in fiscal 2026, driven by domestic demand, private consumption, and steady investment activity.
- RBI policy rate cuts of 100 bps during fiscal 2026 lowered cost of borrowing, supporting consumption revival.
- Banking system non-food credit grew 16.1% YoY, driven by services (19% YoY), personal credit (6.2% YoY), and industry credit (15% YoY).
- Deposit growth for SCBs picked up to 13.5% YoY, improving funding environment.
- Medium-term growth prospects remain positive, supported by structural reforms and policy measures, though global tariff uncertainty and geopolitical developments could weigh on outlook.
- RBI projects GDP growth for fiscal 2027 at approximately 6.9%, supported by strong domestic demand, services sector, higher manufacturing capacity utilisation, and government measures to boost domestic manufacturing.
- RBI projects CPI inflation for fiscal 2027 at 4.6%, with upside pressure from higher global energy prices and concerns of below-normal monsoon; core inflation remains benign.
- Ongoing West Asia conflict poses heightened uncertainty, potential supply-chain disruptions, and upward pressure on energy and commodity prices.
- Rupee depreciation of ~10.9% during fiscal 2026 and decline in equity markets (Sensex -7.06%) reflect external headwinds.
- Bank expects to continue participating in opportunities by leveraging market standing and prioritising long-term sustainable value creation.

The Bank continues to make investments in technology and cybersecurity as part of its ongoing operational resilience and delivery system enhancements.
